Continue study · Wealth → future conditions

Philanthropy as Continuation

Philanthropic continuation is strongest when it funds the conditions for new creators to build authority—not when it requires them to reproduce a founder’s style or gratitude.

Read the exhibition

00

The proposition

Legacy philanthropy can fund education, apprenticeships, archives, conservation, research, tools, space, legal support, production, exhibitions, and unrestricted time. It can also centralize taste, demand imitation, collect beneficiary stories, underpay teaching labor, or convert public generosity into perpetual brand advertising. A school, foundation, company, donor-advised vehicle, prize, or direct grant carries different legal, tax, governance, and accountability questions.

The institutional design starts with the barrier experienced by creators, not the founder’s desired monument. UNESCO’s textile safeguarding work emphasizes knowledge transmission in a specific cultural context; labor and education sources make clear that learning and craft exist within economic conditions. A credible program defines who holds cultural authority, how participants are paid and selected, what rights they retain, which data are collected, how decisions may be appealed, and what survives after funding ends.

01–04

The institutional sequence

01 · CONDITION

Which barrier is being changed?

Use participant and field evidence to name the constraint—time, space, tools, care, legal access, production, archive, education, market, or safety—without inventing deficit narratives.

PROPOSALS73S88

02 · POWER

Who defines success?

Allocate governance among participants, practitioners, community authorities, staff, independent reviewers, and funder; disclose conflicts and create appeal and correction routes.

PROPOSALS87S88

03 · RIGHT

What do recipients retain?

Separate grant conditions, IP, name and likeness, documentation, data, confidentiality, cultural knowledge, publication, archive, and post-program access.

INFERENCES53S54S88

04 · CONTINUE

What remains when funding stops?

Plan unrestricted assets, maintained tools, open or governed curricula, participant networks, preserved records, successor funding, and an ethical closure route.

PROPOSALS39S65

COUNTERPOINT

What this framework could get wrong

A founder may genuinely expand opportunity while retaining disproportionate agenda power. Participant governance and independent evaluation matter because gratitude is not consent and visibility is not benefit.

FIELDWORK

Do the work now

Use this as a working session, not a score.

  1. Define one barrier with affected creators.
  2. Map money, decision, data, rights, credit, and appeal flows.
  3. Pay participant and practitioner review labor.
  4. Design the program’s closure and asset-return plan before launch.

Reading protocol

Every material statement carries an evidence label and point-of-claim source links. Interpretation is never presented as source fact. Legal sections identify their jurisdiction; state, foreign, contractual, beneficial-ownership, validity, priority, and disputed-fact questions remain counsel-review gates. This exhibition is educational and does not provide legal, conservation, or business advice.
